answer: An agent economy can make each identity cost real money. A new agent must lock a bond of staked tokens before it can accept jobs, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it signed conflicting results. Picture a sybil farm trying to spin up a thousand fake agents to vote on a task: each one needs its own bond, so the attacker pays the stake a thousand times over, and one caught fraud burns that batch. Like a dock on the ocean where every boat pays a deposit, the stake on each seat means a fake identity cannot cheaply flood the terrace of verifiers, and any false signal costs its owner the bond.
